subject: Massachusetts Unemployment Insurance Reform
overview: Host Anna Callahan interviewed guest Molly Kivi regarding structural inequities in Massachusetts' unemployment insurance system. Kivi outlined core problems with the current tax and benefit structures and proposed legislative solutions to stabilize the trust fund and support workers.

items.title: Introduction and Personal Context
items.summary: Anna Callahan introduced Molly Kivi to discuss the importance of unemployment insurance as a social safety net and economic stabilizer in Massachusetts.

items.title: Flaws in the Current Unemployment System
items.summary: Molly Kivi detailed five structural issues, including failure to sustain worker purchasing power, regressive tax burdens on small businesses, the experience rating system, a low wage base cap, and trust fund insolvency.

items.title: Proposed Policy Solutions
items.summary: Molly Kivi outlined solutions including increasing benefit payments for low earners, abolishing experience ratings, taxing full wages, and sharing payroll taxes between employers and employees.

items.title: Legislative Challenges and Public Engagement
items.summary: The speakers discussed resistance to reform from corporate special interest groups and urged residents to contact state representatives to advocate for equitable unemployment policies.
